scope.implementation: R4 internal SQL policy/batch storage, signed cursor batch replay, R3 index lease and expiry cleanup

evidence.finding: Output profiles contain scopes plus identity_version only; no nickname/avatar value.
Source keys validated against ordinary FieldCatalog::definitions; nickname/avatar belong to separate identities directory.
18 discovery source keys exclude nickname, avatar_ref and real_name.
projectBatch reconstructs scopes plus identity_version and strips unrecognized identity fields.
Single-person confirmed display-name reader is not a batch discovery-authorized identity capability.
getIdentity is an owner-only single-person flow; media service does not supply batch discover display identities.

identity_capability.conclusion: Keep R3.1 unchecked. Internal ID/projection/score/replay can progress. Do not loop single-person readers, read native profile tables from recommendation, or substitute real names.

review_plan: Verify SQL draft CAS, immutable published history, active-pointer compare and transaction ownership.
Verify new activation identity on rollback and unchanged-content republish; old batch/cursor must not revive.
Verify typed policy/batch codecs reject malformed/extra/oversized data and sanitize errors including enabled trace arguments.
Verify HMAC cursor length/schema/signature, exact viewer/activity/selection/query/policy/batch/position/time binding and fixed expiry.
Verify each page reauthorizes the whole bounded batch, including off-page revocation, and refuses changed policy/context/source.
Verify fixed index leases, microsecond expiry, bounded cleanup, CAS deletion and concurrent release/cleanup without deleting unexpired generations.
Run independent synthetic memory/SQLite probes only after implementation stabilizes; record source hashes and limitations.

design_notes.index_lifecycle: Implemented fixed lease with default 300 seconds and trusted range 1..900 seconds, without renewal. Creation/expiry use exact UTC integer microseconds. Cleanup captures one trusted clock cutoff, claims only observed expired headers by conditional deletion, and removes child rows in the same transaction. Release follows the same header -> term -> interval lock order. A still-running but expired request fails closed; no promise is made to retain expired work.
design_notes.policy_lifecycle: Policy versions bind draft id, revision and parameter digest. Rollback creates a new draft and activation; SQL history insertion rejects reused historical versions. Actual SQL rollback plus existing-batch replay was independently verified. Commit-time external management/catalog authorization guards remain the responsibility of a future management composition.
design_notes.cursor: Implemented HMAC cursor uses canonical bounded JSON/base64, binds saved batch/context/query/policy/order/position/timestamps, and never renews original expiry. Each page rechecks all <=200 saved people twice and refetches the saved batch before return. This is fixed-batch replay, not a full-activity discovery listing implementation.

findings.summary: Index release originally locked child rows before generation header while cleanup locked header before children, creating a potential MySQL lock-order deadlock.
findings.resolution: Root aligned both deletion paths to header -> term -> interval.
findings.evidence_limit: The lock-order risk is a static SQL transaction finding. Synthetic SQLite verifies correctness and idempotence, not MySQL lock scheduling.

findings.summary: NativeRuleDiscoveryFactory::createBatchReader accepted the HMAC codec as an ordinary parameter; an early actor mismatch with exception arguments enabled retained the codec object and its private key in the error trace.
findings.reproduction: Independent probe used only a synthetic signing-key marker and an unconnected Connection; inspecting the factory error trace found the codec argument serializable with the marker. Zero database/network/model calls.
findings.requested_fix: Mark the cursor-codec capability parameter SensitiveParameter and independently retest the failure path. Consider preventing codec serialization/debug exposure as capability hardening.
findings.resolution: Root added SensitiveParameter to NativeRuleDiscoveryFactory::createBatchReader cursor-codec capability. HmacDiscoveryCursorCodec now refuses serialization and unserialization, marks unserialization data sensitive, and exposes only a redacted debug view.
findings.retest: Four independent final assertions passed; cursor/replay 32 and SQL rollback/batch 21 were rerun after the signing-capability change and remained passing.

independent_probes.coverage: Actual P1/P8 pure request/field policy rejects identity sources; both output reconstruction steps strip unrequested identity values while retaining identity_version.
Exact microsecond deadline; later live generation survives cleanup and late owner release; synthetic lost-header-claim preserves derived rows; untracked legacy rows and external transaction safety.
independent_probes.concurrency_limit: Synthetic SQLite trigger simulates a lost claim. No actual MySQL concurrent scheduling was exercised.

independent_probes.coverage: 200-person varying-page-size traversal; entire batch reauthorized; duplicate/invalid-UTF8 signed payloads rejected; off-page block; cross-actor replay; named-zone DST15-minute vs75-minute expiry; HMAC constructor key redaction.

Actual SQL PolicyLifecycle publication and rollback invalidate prior SQL batches; historical version CAS cannot revive; corrupt draft and checksum-consistent extra batch payload reject; typed codec capacity and error redaction; DST exact time; rollback and caller-transaction ownership.

After correction, early factory authorization failure masks the complete signing capability argument; codec serialization and unserialization reject; debug output redacts the key. Only a synthetic marker was used, with exception arguments enabled and zero DB calls.

conclusion: No unresolved blocking finding for the implemented internal policy/batch persistence, fixed-batch replay, and index lease/cleanup slice. R3.1 identity display remains unavailable under the existing read-only P1/P8 scope; full R3, R4 APIs, M1 and production readiness are not certified.
counting_note: 7 identity capability + 13 index lease/cleanup + 32 cursor/replay + 21 SQL persistence/rollback + 4 signing-capability hardening = 77 distinct final checks. Re-runs after fixes are not counted again. These overlap parent suites and must not be added to the parent regression total.

static_review.layering: Policy and batch persistence, signing, native authority and lease cleanup remain outer adapters. ReadDiscoveryBatch, DTOs and ports remain framework-free. No AI dependency was added.
static_review.factory: NativeRuleDiscoveryFactory creates a fresh batch reader pinned to current actor, selection and published policy. The P1/P8 reader uses that same policy. Cursor capability and Clock are explicitly injected; no key lookup, migration, module boot, synthetic default or HTTP route is introduced.
static_review.data_ownership: Only recommendation-owned policy drafts/publications/pointer, minimal batch IDs/version bindings/times, and derived index lifecycle state are added. No identity display values, original profile rows, contact data, raw source text or credentials are copied into batch storage.
static_review.codec: Closed schema-versioned JSON envelopes use explicit constructors, exact canonical re-encoding, checksums, bounded bytes and typed fields. Unknown payload fields, malformed data and unbound legacy batches are rejected for new use. No PHP unserialize or dynamic class construction is used for persisted payloads.
static_review.concurrency: SQLite exercised revision CAS across adapter instances, atomic rollback, savepoint behavior, expired-header failed-claim preservation and late release. MySQL lock ordering was reviewed statically and aligned; actual multi-connection MySQL contention was not tested.

task_status_advice: R3.7 may be checked only with an explicit qualification to the connected person rule/fixed-batch path and read-time invalidation. Keep R3.1 and public API/full-discovery pagination completion claims separate.
remaining_limits: P1/P8 existing batch APIs do not supply nickname or avatar display values; only identity_version. Completing identity cards requires an authorized upstream batch capability, not configuration changes, singleton loops or native-table fallback.

All executable probes used synthetic in-memory ports or new SQLite :memory: databases. No existing database, real session, MySQL migration/performance test, deployment, model or network call occurred.
Before/after authorization reads are finite observations, not an atomic global permission snapshot or a guarantee to detect every ABA history change.
The SQL policy store does not implement external management/catalog authorization locks through commit. The future management API must supply that guard.

Cleanup is an explicit maintenance capability; scheduler wiring and real operational runbooks are not certified. Legacy index rows without generation metadata are intentionally retained until an explicit maintenance-window migration.
This delivery does not certify HTTP actions, CSRF/error mapping, full-activity ordinary discovery pagination, identity cards, AI, idea targets or full M1 readiness.
HMAC cursors are integrity-protected continuation tokens, not authorization grants or encrypted payloads. Read-time current authority remains required.
